finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The authorization gate combines `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` with `&&`, but `isTeamAdmin` already returns truthy for role ADMIN *or* OWNER, so `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` is equivalent to `isTeamOwner` alone. WHY: Team ADMINs who are not OWNERs are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN and cannot use the new add-guests feature despite the variable being named `isTeamAdminOrOwner`. HOW: Use `||` so either role grants access.
finding.oneSentenceSummary: Team admins denied: `&&` collapses admin-or-owner check to owner-only

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `uniqueGuests` compares the raw, case-preserved `guest` string against a lowercased blacklist and against existing attendee emails with exact equality, and never dedupes the input array. WHY: A blacklisted address can be added by changing its casing (e.g. `Guest@Example.com` bypasses the lowercased entry), a duplicate of an existing attendee can be inserted with different casing, and a client sending `["a@b.com","a@b.com"]` (the server schema has no uniqueness refinement, unlike the dialog) creates duplicate attendee rows. HOW: Normalize emails to lowercase and dedupe before filtering.
finding.oneSentenceSummary: Guest filter is case-sensitive and does not dedupe input emails

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the raw input `guests` array instead of `uniqueGuests`, the set actually persisted as new attendees. WHY: `sendAddGuestsEmails` branches on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to choose `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`, so an existing attendee whose email was re-submitted (or a blacklisted address still present on the booking) is treated as a new guest and receives the wrong notification email. HOW: pass `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` indexes a map that is keyed by directory name, not by slug. WHY: for every app whose `slug` differs from `dirName` (e.g. `googlecalendar` has `slug: "google-calendar"`, `dirName: "googlecalendar"`), the lookup returns `undefined` and the handler returns 404, so credential sync silently fails for those apps; the rest of the codebase indexes this map with `app.dirName` (see `packages/app-store/_appRegistry.ts:17`) or searches by `meta.slug` (`_appRegistry.ts:19-23`). HOW: select `dirName` from `prisma.app` and index with `app.dirName`, or find the entry by `meta.slug === app.slug`.
finding.oneSentenceSummary: Webhook indexes appStoreMetadata by app.slug but the map is keyed by dirName

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `refreshOAuthTokens` is called with `credentialId` (a `Credential.id`) in the `userId` parameter slot. WHY: `refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)` sends `userId` as `calcomUserId` to the credential-sync endpoint, so the app store receives a credential id and resolves the wrong user's credentials for Zoho Bigin. HOW: thread `credential.userId` into `refreshAccessToken` and pass it as the third argument.
finding.oneSentenceSummary: zoho-bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: the sharing branch returns the raw fetch `Response`, while the non-sharing branch returns whatever the caller's `refreshFunction` produced, so the return type is inconsistent across modes. WHY: callers that do not call `.json()` dereference parsed fields on a `Response` — `googlecalendar` reads `res?.data` (a GaxiosResponse field), and `hubspot`/`zohocrm`/`zoho-bigin` read `.data`/`.refresh_token` — so in sharing mode the refresh either throws (googlecalendar: `token.access_token` on `undefined`, swallowed by its catch) or stores bogus data. HOW: normalize the sharing branch to the caller's expected shape (e.g. parse the JSON response and return the token object), or require every caller to use a `Response`-aware helper such as `handleErrorsJson`.
finding.oneSentenceSummary: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response that several callers treat as parsed data

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: the computed schema keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the schema instance's string form, so they collapse to a single non-field key instead of matching token properties. WHY: the intended "assume any property with a number is the expiry" validation never runs, and because `z.object` strips unknown keys by default the numeric expiry (`expires_in`/`expiry_date`) is dropped from the parsed result, causing callers to compute `NaN` expiries (zoom) or repeatedly re-refresh (o365). HOW: use a schema that preserves arbitrary keys, e.g. `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` (or `.catchall(z.unknown())`).
finding.oneSentenceSummary: Dynamic zod keys collapse to one literal, so the expiry field is never captured

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: when the token response has no `refresh_token`, the function writes the literal string `"refresh_token"` into the parsed data. WHY: callers persist this value — o365 spreads `tokenResponse.data` over the stored credential and zoom assigns `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` — so a bogus refresh token is saved, and the next refresh attempt sends the literal `"refresh_token"` and fails; in the sharing path this always triggers because `minimumTokenResponseSchema` never contains a `refresh_token` key. HOW: do not synthesize a placeholder; leave the field absent and have callers fall back to the previously stored `refresh_token`.
finding.improvedCode:
// Do not overwrite with a placeholder; callers should retain the existing refresh_token
  // if the provider did not return a new one.
finding.oneSentenceSummary: parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the literal string "refresh_token" into credentials

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: the new refresh block runs unconditionally (no `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` guard) inside `getClient`, which the constructor calls, and then the jsforce connection is built with the stale `credentialKey.access_token` instead of the freshly parsed token. WHY: every Salesforce calendar service instantiation now issues an extra token POST plus a credential DB write even for installs that do not use credential sharing, while the refreshed access token is discarded for the connection it was fetched for, so the refresh adds latency without affecting the connection. HOW: gate the block behind `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and use `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` (and `instance_url`) when constructing the `jsforce.Connection`; the subsequent `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` check is dead because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` already throws.
finding.oneSentenceSummary: Salesforce always refreshes tokens but builds the connection with the stale access token

finding.label: security
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: the webhook secret is compared with the non-constant-time `!==` operator against a request header. WHY: this secret authorizes creating/overwriting a user's encrypted third-party credentials, so a byte-by-byte comparison leak (timing side channel) can be used to recover it and then inject arbitrary credentials for any `userId`. HOW: compare with a constant-time function such as `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over equal-length buffers, after validating the header is present.
finding.oneSentenceSummary: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality check

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `ZodSafeParseResult` (`{ success, data }`), but this caller assigns that wrapper directly to `key` and persists it, so `credential.key` becomes `{success:true, data:{...}}` instead of the credentials object. WHY: the next request runs `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75), which requires top-level `scope`/`token_type`/`expiry_date`/`access_token`/`refresh_token`, so it throws and permanently breaks Google Calendar token refresh and every subsequent Google Calendar operation for the affected user (the DB row is corrupted). HOW: unwrap the data like the other callers (`office365calendar`/`salesforce`/`zoomvideo` all use `.data`): `const { data: key } = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);`.
finding.oneSentenceSummary: Google credential refresh stores the safeParse wrapper instead of the parsed key

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new `else` branch treats any falsy return from `twilio.scheduleSMS` as a failed send and increments `retryCount`, but `scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` without throwing when the user/team is locked for SMS sending (twilioProvider.ts:92-95). WHY: Reminders for a temporarily locked user/team are counted as two failed attempts and then deleted by the `retryCount > 1` cleanup, so the SMS is never sent once the lock is lifted — silent loss of a scheduled reminder that was never actually attempted. HOW: Only increment `retryCount` for genuine send failures; distinguish the locked/no-op return (e.g. have `scheduleSMS` signal a lock, or check lock state before counting the attempt) instead of treating every falsy result as a failure.

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `catch` block now performs an unguarded `prisma.workflowReminder.update` before logging; if that write throws (transient DB error, or Prisma P2025 when an overlapping cron run already deleted the row via the new `retryCount > 1` cleanup), the exception escapes the for-loop. WHY: A single reminder's failure now aborts processing of all remaining reminders in the batch and returns a 500, whereas before the PR the catch only logged and the loop continued. HOW: Wrap the retry-count update in its own try/catch (or use `updateMany`) so a failed counter update cannot abort the batch.

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new `retryCount > 1` OR branch in `deleteMany` is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, unlike the sibling branch, so the delete now targets reminders of every method. WHY: `retryCount` is a method-agnostic column on the shared `WorkflowReminder` table, so any non-SMS reminder that ever carries a retry count above 1 (a future writer, a data fix, or the WhatsApp flow adopting the same retry mechanism) is silently removed by the SMS cron without being sent. HOW: Hoist `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the top-level `where` and keep only the date/retry conditions in the `OR`.

finding.label: security
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for `raw_html` posts, bypassing the sanitization that `PrettyText.cook` applies (`sanitize: true`, pretty_text.rb:134/169). WHY: `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` renders `raw post.cooked`, so HTML imported from an external feed — whose item bodies can be authored by third parties — executes as script on the forum origin, giving stored XSS. HOW: run the imported markup through the HTML sanitizer before returning it (e.g. sanitize `raw` with `PrettyText`/`HtmlSanitizer`) instead of returning it verbatim.
finding.existingCode: return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]
finding.improvedCode: return PrettyText.sanitize(raw) if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]
finding.oneSentenceSummary: raw_html posts bypass sanitization and are rendered with raw, enabling stored XSS

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `absolutize_urls` treats any `href`/`src` beginning with `/` as relative, but protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/a.png` also begin with `/`. WHY: they get rewritten to `#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/a.png`, producing a broken link/image in every imported post. HOW: skip protocol-relative values (`!href.start_with?('//')`) or prepend the scheme (`"#{uri.scheme}:#{href}"`) for the `//` case.
finding.oneSentenceSummary: Protocol-relative URLs are mangled into invalid absolute URLs

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `i.content.scrub` is called with no nil guard; simple-rss exposes only the XML elements present, so RSS 2.0 feeds that carry `<description>` (no `<content>`) yield nil and `.scrub` raises NoMethodError. WHY: the whole poll job aborts mid-feed and, with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the remaining items are never imported. HOW: fall back across the possible fields and coerce, e.g. `CGI.unescapeHTML((i.content || i.description).to_s.scrub)`.
finding.existingCode: content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)
finding.improvedCode: content = CGI.unescapeHTML((i.content || i.description).to_s.scrub)
finding.oneSentenceSummary: poll_feed crashes when a feed item has no <content> element

finding.label: performance
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `perform_retrieve` synchronously runs the full feed poll (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`) whenever an embed URL is not yet known and feed polling is enabled. WHY: each new embed triggers a full feed HTTP fetch plus an import/lookup for every feed item — O(feed size) DB work per embed — duplicating the hourly scheduled job instead of a single existence check. HOW: rely on the already-scheduled PollFeed job (or enqueue it) and only fall back to `fetch_http` for the requested URL, rather than polling the entire feed inline.
finding.existingCode:
if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?
  Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})
  return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?
end
finding.improvedCode:
if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?
  Jobs.enqueue(:poll_feed, {})
  return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?
end
finding.oneSentenceSummary: Full feed poll runs synchronously on every embed miss

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `best.html.erb` closes the header `if/else` with `<%- end if %>`, but Ruby's `if` modifier requires a condition expression that is not present (the `if`/`else` was already closed by the preceding branch). WHY: the ERB either fails to compile (the embed frame renders nothing) or silently consumes the next output expression as the modifier's condition, so the header markup is generated by accident; grep confirms every other ERB in the repo uses a plain `<% end %>`. HOW: replace `<%- end if %>` with `<%- end %>`.
finding.existingCode: <%- end if %>
finding.oneSentenceSummary: Embed view closes its header if/else with a conditionless `end if`

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: this spec asserts `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)`/`retrieve` when no embed is found, but `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...)` and never references `TopicRetriever` directly. WHY: the Mocha expectation is never satisfied, so the spec fails, and the actual asynchronous retrieval path exercised by the controller is not covered. HOW: assert `Jobs.expects(:enqueue).with(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, or change the controller to call `TopicRetriever.new(embed_url, no_throttle: ...).retrieve` if synchronous behavior is intended.

TopicEmbed.expects(:topic_id_for_embed).returns(nil)
        retriever = mock
        TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)
        retriever.expects(:retrieve)
        get :best, embed_url: embed_url
finding.improvedCode:
TopicEmbed.expects(:topic_id_for_embed).returns(nil)
        Jobs.expects(:enqueue).with(:retrieve_topic, has_entries(embed_url: embed_url))
        get :best, embed_url: embed_url
finding.oneSentenceSummary: Controller spec expects TopicRetriever but controller enqueues a job

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: the migration adds a `NOT NULL` column with a default (`add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`) to the hot `posts` table. WHY: on PostgreSQL versions before 11 this performs a full table rewrite while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, blocking all reads and writes to `posts` for the duration of the deploy on a large forum. HOW: add the column as nullable/without a default, backfill it in batches, then apply the default and NOT NULL constraint in a separate step.
finding.existingCode: add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false
finding.improvedCode:
add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer
    # backfill in batches, then:
    change_column_default :posts, :cook_method, 1
    change_column_null :posts, :cook_method, false, 1
finding.oneSentenceSummary: NOT NULL default column added to hot posts table rewrites it under exclusive lock

finding.llmPrompt: WHAT: `perform_retrieve` synchronously runs the full feed poll (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`) whenever an embed URL is not yet known and feed polling is enabled. WHY: each new embed triggers a full feed HTTP fetch plus an import/lookup for every feed item — O(feed size) DB work per embed — duplicating the hourly scheduled job instead of a single existence check. HOW: rely on the already-scheduled PollFeed job (or enqueue it) and only fall back to `fetch_http` for the requested URL, rather than polling the entire feed inline.

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: the migration inserts the legacy `embeddable_hosts` setting values with raw SQL, bypassing the `EmbeddableHost#before_validation` that strips `http(s)://` and paths, so a stored value like `http://eviltrout.com` is persisted verbatim. HOW: normalize each value before inserting, e.g. `h = h.sub(/^https?:\/\//, '').sub(/\/.*$/, '')` (or create via `EmbeddableHost`) so stored hosts match the lookup.

HOW: emit `$val + 1` for the two legacy box properties and keep `$val` for the modern `order`/`-ms-flex-order`/`-webkit-order`.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `validateUploadedFile` now uses a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB limit instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so the client-side size check ignores the configured `max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb`. WHY: attachments are never downsized server-side (the controller loop is guarded by `FileHelper.is_image?`), so a file between the configured limit and 10MB passes the client check and is then rejected by `UploadValidator#maximum_file_size`, replacing immediate client feedback with a server round-trip and an error; sites that lowered the limit (e.g. 1MB) are no longer respected on the client. HOW: keep the site setting for non-image types and only raise the ceiling for images, e.g. `var maxSizeKB = type === 'image' ? 10 * 1024 : Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'];`.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts by one page whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100 members with limit 50 reports 3 pages). WHY: `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to this inflated value, so the Next arrow stays enabled on the true last page and clicking it requests `offset = user_count`, rendering an empty member list. HOW: use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.
finding.oneSentenceSummary: totalPages overcounts by one page when user_count is a multiple of limit

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `group.users.delete(user_id)` removes the join rows through the `has_many :through` association, which issues a bulk delete and skips the `counter_cache: "user_count"` callback defined on `GroupUser`. WHY: unlike the previous removal path (`Group#remove`, which called `destroy` on each `GroupUser`), the counter is never decremented, so `groups.user_count` — surfaced by `BasicGroupSerializer` in the admin group list — becomes stale after a member is removed. HOW: delete the join records in a way that fires the callback, e.g. `group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).each(&:destroy)`.
finding.existingCode: group.users.delete(user_id)
finding.improvedCode: group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).each(&:destroy)
finding.oneSentenceSummary: remove_member bypasses the group_users counter cache, leaving user_count stale

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `add_members` calls `group.add(user)` (i.e. `users.push`) for every parsed username without checking whether the user is already a member, and `group_users` has a UNIQUE index on (group_id, user_id). WHY: adding a username that already belongs to the group attempts a duplicate join insert and raises a unique-violation, returning a 500 instead of a clean response; the removed `usernames=` setter avoided this by computing `expected - current`. HOW: skip users already in the group, e.g. `group.add(user) unless group.users.exists?(user.id)`.
finding.existingCode:
usernames.split(",").each do |username|
      if user = User.find_by_username(username)
        group.add(user)
      end
    end
finding.improvedCode:
usernames.split(",").each do |username|
      if user = User.find_by_username(username)
        group.add(user) unless group.users.exists?(user.id)
      end
    end
finding.oneSentenceSummary: add_members inserts duplicate group_users rows and raises a unique violation

finding.label: performance
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: the `members` action takes `limit` directly from `params[:limit]` with no upper bound and applies it to every group, not just automatic ones. WHY: any user who can view a group can pass `limit=10000000` (or a negative value) and force the server to load and serialize the entire member set, an unbounded load that can exhaust memory/DB on large groups; the old code only paginated automatic groups. HOW: clamp the values, e.g. `limit = [[(params[:limit] || 50).to_i, 1].max, 100].min` and `offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max`.
finding.existingCode:
limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i
    offset = params[:offset].to_i
finding.improvedCode:
limit = [[(params[:limit] || 50).to_i, 1].max, 100].min
    offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max
finding.oneSentenceSummary: members endpoint accepts an unbounded limit parameter

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The fallback chain returned here is derived from the mutable `SiteSetting.default_locale`, but I18n's accelerator cache stores the resolved fallback string under a key that omits the fallback chain (`"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`, lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:71-76). WHY: For any user locale that is missing a key, the value cached at that moment is the then-current `SiteSetting.default_locale` translation, and because nothing resets `@cache` when the setting changes (only `I18n.reload!` at boot clears it), an admin changing `default_locale` leaves users served the old fallback language for hot keys until the 300-entry LRU evicts them. HOW: Make the cached value depend on the fallback chain, e.g. append the fallback list to the accelerator cache key, or reset `I18n`'s cache when `SiteSetting.default_locale` is saved.

WHY: In non-request processes (Sidekiq jobs via app/jobs/base.rb:151, mailers via app/services/post_alerter.rb:138) the default/`:en` locales are never preloaded, so when `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` falls back it calls `super(fallback, ...)` against an unloaded locale and yields a missing translation — the exact failure this feature is meant to remove. HOW: Load the fallback chain in a shared boot/worker entry point (e.g. call `I18n.ensure_loaded!(SiteSetting.default_locale)` / `:en` alongside `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale` in app/jobs/base.rb) instead of relying on the controller filter.

finding.suggestionContent: The analysis notes a genuine defect: the cached fallback chain is not invalidated when SiteSetting.default_locale changes. Because the fallback list is memoized/derived from the default locale (FallbackLocaleList#[] at i18n.rb:13-18, installed at i18n.rb:24), changing SiteSetting.default_locale at runtime leaves the previously computed fallback chain in place, so translations continue to fall back to the stale locale. (This is called out as an already-captured finding and is not restated in detail in the analysis.)

finding.improvedCode:
# Invalidate the fallback chain whenever the default locale setting changes,
# e.g. subscribe to SiteSetting.default_locale changes and reset the cached
# fallback list / I18n.fallbacks so subsequent lookups use the new chain.
class FallbackLocaleList
  def [](locale)
    [locale.to_sym, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym]
  end
end

I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new
# ensure cache invalidation on SiteSetting.default_locale change

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: after taking the exclusive `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`, the code never re-checks `entryPointAssetsCache`, so the double-checked-locking fast path is only half implemented. WHY: every caller that missed the unlocked fast-path read (all concurrent callers during the initial cache-miss burst, and — because `result` stays nil on read failure — every request when the manifest is missing/misconfigured) re-runs `readWebAssetsFromFile` + JSON decode serially while holding a process-wide exclusive lock, serializing all index/frontend-settings/recovery requests instead of recomputing once. HOW: re-verify the cache immediately after acquiring the write lock and return the now-populated value.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The async legacy-write goroutines derive their context with `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, …)` from the request-scoped `ctx` (lines 50-57, 108-114, 134-141, 161-167). WHY: net/http and the k8s apiserver cancel the request context when the handler returns, so the derived 10s timeout context is already canceled and `d.Legacy.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection` can be aborted immediately — the 'safe measure' legacy write mode 3 depends on does not reliably complete, risking silent divergence between the two stores. HOW: Detach from the request lifecycle, e.g. `context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), time.Second*10, errors.New("legacy create timeout"))` (or a background context), so the legacy write survives handler completion.
finding.existingCode:
go func() {
		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, errors.New("legacy create timeout"))
		defer cancel()

		startLegacy := time.Now()
		_, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, createValidation, options)
		d.recordLegacyDuration(errObjectSt != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)
	}()
finding.improvedCode:
go func() {
		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), time.Second*10, errors.New("legacy create timeout"))
		defer cancel()

		startLegacy := time.Now()
		_, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, createValidation, options)
		d.recordLegacyDuration(errObjectSt != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)
	}()

	ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)

	ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log)

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The async legacy-write goroutines no longer log the error returned by `d.Legacy.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection`, so a failed legacy write is silently swallowed (only the `is_error` metric label survives). HOW: log `errObjectSt` before recording the metric in each goroutine (e.g. `log.Error(errObjectSt, "unable to create object in legacy storage")`).

finding.oneSentenceSummary: Legacy write failures are silently swallowed in the async goroutines

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The legacy write now runs inside a bare `go func()` with no `recover`, whereas it previously ran inside the request handler that the apiserver wraps with panic recovery. WHY: an unrecovered panic in any goroutine terminates the entire Grafana process, so a panic in the legacy storage path — previously a single failed request — now crashes every in-flight request. HOW: wrap the goroutine body in `defer func(){ if r := recover(); r != nil { log.Error(nil, "panic in legacy write", "recover", r) } }()`.

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The newly added s.search.TotalDocs() call runs concurrently with cache writes: the watch goroutine started a few lines earlier (search.go:207) and concurrent Search RPCs can invoke BuildIndex, which writes b.cache[key] at bleve.go:137-139, while bleveBackend.TotalDocs (bleve.go:144-154) iterates b.cache without holding cacheMu. WHY: Concurrent map iteration and map write is an unrecoverable Go runtime fatal error that crashes the whole process (not a recoverable panic) the moment a watch event or search request lands in the window between the goroutine start and this call. HOW: Make bleveBackend.TotalDocs take cacheMu.RLock() (like GetIndex does) before ranging over b.cache, or snapshot the values under lock.

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The coarse cacheMu.Lock() that wrapped the entire BuildIndex body was removed, leaving only the cache-map write at the end locked; BuildIndex is now called concurrently for the same key (getOrCreateIndex in search.go:287 only checks GetIndex before building, and both Search and handleEvent call it). WHY: Two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource now run simultaneously — for a file-backed index both call bleve.New on the same directory (dir = Root/namespace/resource.group, line 97), so one build can fail on the directory lock, and both execute a full unbounded ListIterator scan (Limit 1000000000000 in search.go:328), doubling DB and index-build load; the last cache write wins and the other caller keeps an index that is no longer in the cache. HOW: Serialize per key (e.g. a keyed single-flight/lock) so concurrent requests for the same uncached key share one build instead of racing.
finding.existingCode:
b.cacheMu.Lock()
	b.cache[key] = idx
	b.cacheMu.Unlock()
	return idx, nil
finding.oneSentenceSummary: Lock narrowing lets concurrent same-key builds race and duplicate work

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: the reader thread is never joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` runs, so the assertion can execute while the reader is still mid-request. WHY: the NPE the test is meant to catch may be recorded after the assertion, letting the test pass even when the concurrent-access bug is present (false negative), and because the thread is non-daemon and only terminates via `deletedAll`, a throw in the `remove()` loop (which skips `deletedAll.set(true)`) leaves it spinning forever and hangs/leaks the thread. HOW: keep a reference to the thread, and after `deletedAll.set(true)` call `thread.join()` before asserting.

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `start` (common-prefix length) and `end` (common-suffix length) are computed by two independent loops, so when the prefix and suffix regions overlap `start + end` can exceed `sanitized.length()` (or `value.length()`), and `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` / `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`. WHY: the whole build/install step crashes instead of reporting the offending key whenever the sanitized and normalized strings share an overlapping prefix/suffix (e.g. `value="aab"`, `sanitized="ab"`), aborting the verifier. HOW: bound the suffix loop by the remaining room after the prefix, e.g. `int limit = Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start;` and loop `while (end < limit && value.charAt(value.length()-end-1) == sanitized.charAt(sanitized.length()-end-1)) end++;`.

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `getClientsWithPermission` adds `resource.getName()` for every resource returned by `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...)`, but the "all-clients" type resource has name `"Clients"`, which is not a client id. WHY: the only caller, `AvailableRoleMappingResource.getRoleIdsWithPermissions` (line 230), treats each returned string as a client id and calls `realm.getClientById(cid).getRolesStream()`, so when the admin holds the scope on all clients the set contains `"Clients"` and the endpoint throws NullPointerException; conversely, per-client resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never get `setType(...)`, so individual client grants are never returned. HOW: skip the resource whose name equals the resource-type name (or filter by matching the client id) before adding it to `granted`.
finding.oneSentenceSummary: getClientsWithPermission returns the type-resource name "Clients" as a client id

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: the removal listener is now gated on `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1) while the calls it guards route through `management(...)`, which returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled. WHY: with both flags enabled `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...)` resolves to `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, so removing a client/role/group still fails with an unhandled exception despite the new guard. HOW: gate on the V2 flag as well (e.g. skip when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled) so the V2 evaluator is never invoked for cleanup.

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` (and `hasPermission(String)`) treats every `Permission` returned by `root.evaluatePermission(...)` as a grant for the resource being checked, without verifying `permission.getResourceId()` matches `resource.getId()` — the guard that `UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission` applies (UserPermissionsV2.java:135). WHY: if the evaluator returns a permission whose scope matches but which targets a different resource, an admin with a permission on one resource is granted the scope on another client, producing an over-permissive authorization decision (the check is only ever made more permissive by removing the filter). HOW: skip permissions whose resource id differs from the evaluated resource before inspecting scopes.
finding.oneSentenceSummary: hasPermission ignores which resource a returned permission targets

finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` (and `hasPermission(String)`) treats every `Permission` returned by `root.evaluatePermission(...)` as a grant for the resource being checked, without verifying `permission.getResourceId()` matches `resource.getId()` — the guard that `UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission` applies (UserPermissionsV2.java:135). WHY: if the evaluator returns a permission whose scope matches but which targets a different resource, an admin with a permission on one resource is granted the scope on another client, producing an over-permissive authorization decision (the check is only ever made more permissive by removing the filter). HOW: skip permissions whose resource id differs from the evaluated resource before inspecting scopes.

WHY: toggling BROKER_PUBLIC on a realm-level IDP leaves organizationId unchanged, so neither branch invalidates the .idp.login.ORG_ONLY cache and getForLogin(ORG_ONLY, null) keeps serving the stale ID set. finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: In `join`, the new `if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the process loop before `process.terminate()` is reached. WHY: When `next_step.join(timeout)` consumes the whole deadline (or a process hangs), no flusher process is force-terminated — the previous single-process code always called `terminate()`, so this drops the safety net that reaps a hung flusher during shutdown/rebalance (a hung process never observes `stopped` and leaks until interpreter exit). HOW: Move the `terminate()` call so it runs even when the deadline is exhausted, e.g. drop the `break` and rely on the wait loop's own deadline check, or call `process.terminate()` before breaking.

finding.llmPrompt: WHAT: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates the default a single time at module import, so every `AssignmentSource` built via `from_integration` (or any construction without an explicit `queued`) shares the process-start timestamp rather than the moment the assignment was queued. WHY: `queued` is silently wrong/stale for the lifetime of the worker, so any freshness, dedup, or ordering logic keyed on it (and the serialized value round-tripped through `to_dict`/`from_dict`) will misbehave. HOW: use a default factory so the timestamp is computed per instance: `from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field` and `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.
